verify_exec.schema: language python|node; code<=8000; stdin<=8000; claim<=300; timeoutSeconds 1-20
verify_exec.isolation: bwrap --die-with-parent --unshare-user --unshare-pid --unshare-ipc --unshare-uts --unshare-cgroup --new-session --ro-bind / / --dev /dev [--proc /proc|--tmpfs /proc] --tmpfs /tmp --bind <tmp> /tmp/work --chdir /tmp/work; launcher sets RLIMIT_NPROC=64, RLIMIT_FSIZE=8MiB, RLIMIT_CPU, RLIMIT_AS=512MiB (python only); output<=8000 chars; killpg on timeout
verify_exec.isolationMatrix: quyết định chủ máy #6423 (02/10): KHÔNG tách net (snippet dùng netns của box theo công tắc firewall), '/' vẫn --ro-bind nên repo ĐỌC được mà không ghi được, không còn tmpfs che ROOT, scratch = tmpfs /tmp + temp dir bind tại /tmp/work; receipt thêm scratchRoot + scratch [{path, bytes}] (<=20 mục, quét đúng temp dir của lượt gọi, trần 200 mục)

repoReadOnly.read: exit 0, 1459 dòng của worker.py đọc được trong box

verify_exec.promptHardening: quyết định #6423: hợp đồng finding (EN+VI), mô tả tool verify_exec, REVIEW/RESEARCH_REVIEW/PLAN_REVIEW instructions và WORK_REVIEWER_NOTE nói rõ repo ĐỌC được read-only, scratch ở /tmp/work, ra mạng được, và một finding chặn phải trích toolCallId của call trong chính lượt hoặc chữ ký verify:<codeHash>; tham chiếu văn xuôi bị hạ. SOP mục G thêm yêu cầu main dẫn receipt của reviewer.

no bwrap on PATH -> VERIFY_EXEC_UNAVAILABLE, no fallback (unit test)

verify_exec.dockerFinding: bwrap cần user namespace: profile Docker mặc định chặn ('No permissions to create new namespace'), seccomp=unconfined một mình vẫn hỏng ('Failed to make / slave'), seccomp+apparmor unconfined thì chạy (procMode 'tmpfs'). verify_exec.health: GET /health?probe=verify refreshes runtime.verifyExecStatus; /health always returns verifyExec

findingContract.uncitedRevise: coverage entry revise whose findings were all downgraded -> status 'unverified' + contractError WORK_FINDING_UNCITED; a revise with no valid blocking finding cannot pass
findingContract.knownNuance: a coverage entry with target=criterion keeps 'revise' (it is routed to main as inputConflicts, the W6.1.1 contract) even when its linked findings were downgraded; in that case the check status can stay 'revise' with blocking=[] and no contractError
findingContract.legacy: reports without a findings list keep the old semantics (policy-10 records and legacy fixtures)

nativeProbe.design: 3 cases x 2 runs; fixture artifact, no main model, no Build; reviewer tools include verify_exec (real bwrap on the host). Rows 1-5 come from the first invocation, row 6 from a --resume invocation after the probe itself crashed at fixture setup (git commit "nothing to commit" when reusing a folder); both invocations carry the same sourceManifest, and the manifest matches fe01f19 exactly. Rows were re-scored from the on-disk databases (newest work_checks doc per folder) with the same oracle: identical verdicts.
nativeProbe.oracle: every surviving blocking finding cites a receipt observed in THIS admission; a numeric claim cites a verify_exec receipt; a true finding stays blocking; a false one never blocks

attempts.contractError: Invalid JSON coverage; every assigned id needs status and evidence. Revised A criteria must explicitly set target=artifact or target=criterion.

honestFailures: Space Bunny STILL never called verify_exec in any of the 6 runs (verifyExecCalls = 0/6) although the tool was in the child tool list and the prompt now demands it for numeric claims — the model-behaviour half of the oracle is not fixed by prompt text.

Because no verify_exec receipt exists, the numeric half of the oracle is vacuous in these runs: the surviving blocking findings carry no numeric token per NUMERIC_CLAIM_RE, so numericCited=true does not prove a measured number. The artifact receipt (artifact:<id>@<contentHash>) is the only receipt form the model used; the oracle counts it as known because the backend accepts it.

Prompt hardening did change the citation behaviour: downgrades fell from 7/20 findings (35%, all UNKNOWN_RECEIPT) to 5/29 (17%, 3 UNKNOWN_RECEIPT + 2 SELF_REFUTED) and the model now says in its own report that it downgraded a finding because it had no verify_exec receipt.

The false-positive control case failed in BOTH runs this time (side-remark #1 and #2 both ended revise with a blocking finding): the reviewer blocked on "the artifact does not define dialect/quoting/lineterminator" and "no pytest output in the workspace", i.e. on missing evidence rather than on the wrong side remark. Pre-change that case produced unverified/no blocking in the one run that survived.

csv-error-type premise: Python 3.12 does NOT raise csv.Error for a NUL inside a str for csv.reader (measured with verify_exec: ['a\x00b'] parses fine); the surviving finding is about the artifact citing "đúng như tài liệu mô tả" while docs/source.md names no exception.
N is 6 rows; two of the six (nfd-count) took ~520 s each and one earlier pre-change row was lost to a provider stream interruption, so the rate is a signal, not a benchmark.

deliverable.lookup: Answer <=120 words + Sources opened + Unverified; no options or recommendation
deliverable.researchBrief: research node with depth=brief: Answer, Verified facts, Gaps, <=400 words, no options section
deliverable.proportionalNote: plan/design deliverables append a proportional note (findings <=8, claim <=300 chars)

producerQuality.unsourcedClaim: answer_knowledge(): a claim naming a path/URL that was not opened marks the binding verification='unverified' and error='WORK_CLAIM_UNSOURCED: <path>'
producerQuality.reviewedSet: finish_verify() on verdict ok writes run['reviewedSet'] = {wholeBinding, artifacts[], claims[], reviewedAt, verdict}; result() returns stale=true when the whole binding or a reviewed artifact hash changed
producerQuality.finalClaims: runtime.final_claim_notices() at main turn end emits work_notice {type:'unreviewed_claims'} (non-blocking) for tokens outside reviewedSet.claims that carry no 'chưa kiểm/unverified' label
producerQuality.mainLanguage: SOP section G requires the owner-facing commentary in the owner language (Vietnamese with accents)

lookupProbe.design: A/B on the same fixture: legacy arm = node without taskKind (pre-W6.2 behaviour), lookup arm = taskKind=lookup; 1 run each
lookupProbe.oracleNote: strict raw count: the Answer part (everything before the sources heading) must be <=120 words; the lookup arm measured 122 raw / 119 without headings, so the strict oracle fails by 2 words while the shape (sections, length class) matches the contract.

Muốn quay lại mặc định an toàn hơn: xoá 2 dòng security_opt, tool tự fail closed VERIFY_EXEC_UNAVAILABLE (không có fallback chạy không cách ly).

Model behaviour after the #6423 prompt hardening (6 rows): the model still never calls verify_exec (0/6) and now blocks on the false-positive control case in both runs, but it cites real receipts more often (downgrades 7/20 -> 5/29 findings) and self-downgrades findings it cannot back. W10 should keep tracking verifyExecCalls and the downgrade/false-positive rate; prompt text alone did not make the model measure.
